roles: and the tests that prove they work
hero_pitch: Hi, I'm Nikhil. I learn a subject by building something real with it and then trying my hardest to break it. What's here is thirty end-to-end projects — analytics, data engineering, machine learning, LLM systems and test engineering — where every single number is scored against a known ground truth, and the results that proved me wrong are written up as carefully as the ones that proved me right.
bio: I taught myself to build by being stubborn about one question: how do I actually know this works? It's easy to write down a number that flatters the thing you made. I got interested in the harder habit — planting a known answer in the data first, then grading my own work against it, and reporting the result even when it embarrasses me.

I did my BCA in Patna and my MCA at CHRIST University in Bengaluru. For eight months I worked a Google Pay voice-support process at Cognizant on US-shift hours — and, oddly, that's where I learned what data is really for. Working complaint queues teaches you that a metric is a promise someone is accountable for, that an average hides the cases that actually hurt, and that a dashboard number is only as good as the definition nobody wrote down.

So I went all in on building. Over the past year I've shipped thirty public, reproducible projects and written a full notebook for each — thirty of them, nearly two thousand pages — because writing it up is how I find out which parts I didn't actually understand. Several of these projects exist only because the checkable version of the answer disagreed with the obvious one.

I'm the kind of person who reads the error message, reaches for the trivial baseline before the fancy model, and would rather ship an honest 0.18 than a flattering 1.00. If that's the kind of care you want on a team, I'd love to talk.

journey.title: Eight months in the real world
journey.body: Worked a Google Pay voice-support process on US-shift hours. Running complaint queues taught me, bluntly, what data is for — that behind every metric is a person it's accountable to.

journey.title: All in on building
